result_summary.result:
No devboard data dir in this scratch session, so that's a silent no-op as designed — fine, doesn't block presenting findings.

## Findings

**Why Next/Someday are invisible today:** the dashboard has no concept of a ticket at all — it only reads YAML task files from `DEVBOARD_DATA/<repo>/*.yaml`. Those files are exclusively created by `worklog start` (`internal/devboard.OnStart`, `worklog/internal/cli/start.go:104`), which only fires when a ticket moves into `## Now`. `worklog add` (what creates Next/Someday entries) never touches the devboard dir. So "no task file" and "not started" are the same thing by construction — Next/Someday tickets simply don't exist from devboard's point of view.

**The data devboard would need already exists and is already in reach:**
- `worklog status --json` (`worklog/internal/cli/status.go`) emits Now/Waiting/Next/Someday as structured blocks (id, title, type, parent, repo, tags, acceptance, ...) straight from the same `model.WorkDoc` the CLI itself uses.
- The devboard container already mounts the whole worklog data dir read-only at `/worklog` (`devboard/compose.yaml:8`) — `WORK.md` sits right next to `notes/` and `FEEDBACK.md`, which `server.py` already reads from that mount. No new mount is needed.

**There's an exact precedent for this shape of feature:** the Friction panel. `FEEDBACK.md` is a worklog-owned file with no per-task YAML involvement; `server.py` parses it itself (`_parse_feedback`, deliberately permissive, skips unknown fields) and renders it as a standalone read-only band; the only interaction is a copy-command button, never a live write, because the worklog mount is read-only. `devboard/test_server.py` pins that parser against the Go format.

**Why a task file per backlog item is the wrong shape:** `devboard/schema.md`'s ownership model treats a task file as disposable *in-flight* telemetry — phase tracker, resume button, plan/scorecard — created deliberately only at `start`. Forcing `worklog add` to also drop a task file would blur "started" vs "not started" (the exact distinction the schema currently encodes), litter the data dir with near-empty files for every backlog idea, and need new bookkeeping to delete/rename them as tickets move Next → Someday → Now → done.

## Recommendation

Mirror the Friction-panel pattern: teach `server.py` to parse `WORK.md` directly (a small line-oriented parser mirroring `internal/parse/work.go`'s regexes — section headers, `- [ ] **ID** — Title`, indented `**Field**:` metadata) and expose Next/Someday as a new read-only "Backlog" band in `/api/tasks`, rendered as its own collapsed fold (like Friction) grouped by the block's `Repo:` field to stay consistent with the rest of the board. Each entry shows ID/title/type badge/tags, no detail page (there's nothing to drill into pre-start), and optionally a copy-`worklog start <id>` button — same "copy command, never write" rule the friction/resume buttons already follow, since the worklog mount is read-only.

This needs zero Go-side or schema changes, no new mount, and follows a pattern this codebase has already chosen once. The real cost is a second WORK.md parser to keep in sync with the Go grammar — same tradeoff already accepted for `FEEDBACK.md`, and the grammar is small (a handful of regexes) and only needs a read path.

**Alternatives considered and why not:** a `worklog reindex`-style command that snapshots Next/Someday into a JSON side-file avoids the second parser but adds a new write path that must fire on every `add`/`start`/`wait`/`done` to avoid staleness — more moving parts than a live read. Per-ticket task files for backlog items were ruled out above.

This is a spike, so no code changed. Want me to close `adb-devboard-backlog-visibility` with this as the summary, or open it up for more digging (e.g., a rough diff sketch of the WORK.md parser mirror) first?
